source.title: Probing Knowledge Holes in Unlearned LLMs
source.authors: Myeongseob Ko; Just Anh Hoang; Charles Fleming; Ming Jin; Ruo-Xi Jia

page_placements.theme: Off-target effects on retained knowledge near the target (ripple, knowledge holes, over-generalization) that general benchmarks miss

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unintended losses of benign knowledge after unlearning and attempts to restore those losses. It does not test whether attacks recover the targeted knowledge that was meant to be forgotten, or whether that knowledge remains in the weights.
record.gate_note: The main results compare answer quality on benign adjacent and latent prompts before and after unlearning. These concern collateral knowledge loss, not recovery of the targeted forgotten knowledge in versions A–F. The mitigation experiments fine-tune on identified benign prompts and likewise do not test recovery of targeted knowledge. Standard benchmarks, diversity scores, and harmscores do not measure the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study is about collateral benign-knowledge loss, not recovery. But its one-shot mitigation fine-tunes an LLMU-unlearned Mistral-7B only on benign, forget-set-filtered adjacent/latent prompts. It then measures harmscore on the original forgetting set, which rises from 0.00 to 0.10 (GD) and 0.90 (KL). That is an incidental result on version B: relearning on loosely related benign data revives the unlearned harmful content. All other results concern collateral loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Authors conclude unlearning creates knowledge holes in benign adjacent and latent knowledge that static benchmarks miss. They add that mitigation by relearning identified holes faces a persistent trade-off: it revives harmful content (one-shot) or creates new holes (iterative). They call for dynamic, model-dependent evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Applies four named unlearning algorithms using their described approaches, with the stated model and dataset pairings; RMU uses a checkpoint released by its authors. The study does not implement or test the recovery-attack recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The degree of observed collateral loss varies by unlearning method and by adjacent versus latent prompt set; additional full-parameter LLMU results vary across judges and report standard deviations.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearned models (LLMU, GAKL, NPOGD on PKU; RMU on WMDP-Bio) answer benign adjacent prompts much worse than the pretrained model (e.g. RMU 7.848→4.495), while MMLU/ARC/TruthfulQA barely move. RL-searched latent prompts reach up to 98.7% score-1 responses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning causes collateral loss of benign knowledge that static benchmarks miss.

fits_no_version.finding: Restoring identified knowledge holes by one-shot or iterative retain-set augmentation is incomplete and exposes new holes. Iterative re-unlearning keeps harmscore 0 but DLP stays near 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repairing collateral unlearning damage trades off against harm suppression or creates new holes.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The main evaluations use LLM-based response-quality judgments. The paper notes that RL search depends on hyperparameters and can require extensive tuning; the full-parameter robustness results use three seeds and three generation runs. These limitations concern its knowledge-hole evaluation, not recovery tests.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include general benchmark scores, harmscore-only checkpoint results, diversity metrics, qualitative examples, or the table of response-quality criteria: they do not assess recovery of targeted forgotten knowledge or add a separately relevant result beyond the collateral-loss rows. Table 4's starting LLMU line is represented as the baseline for its mitigation rows rather than as a separate intervention result.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance (no WMDP accuracy reported), and robustness to attacks. Only harmscore 0 on the forgetting set and general benchmarks are reported.
Relearning on unrelated data or on a subset of forgotten facts; any test on RMU/WMDP; other methods (GAKL, NPOGD); targeted accuracy rather than harmscore.
Entire version: no activation-direction ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
Entire version: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
Entire version: no robust counter-method proposed or tested.

missing.what: Harmscore on the forgetting set after one-shot mitigation at steps 600/800/1000: KL 0.80/0.90/0.80, GD 0.12/0.10/0.08. This shows the B-relevant revival is stable across checkpoints.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/none classification misses that one-shot mitigation is effectively a benign-data relearning experiment. Its harmscore on the forgetting set rises to 0.90 (KL), which bears on B even though the authors frame it as a utility trade-off. Harmscore is an LLM-judged rate of harmful compliance, not targeted-knowledge accuracy. The mitigation prompts were filtered to exclude forget-set content, so they count as loosely related data. The collateral-loss results speak to A's 'keeps general ability' only loosely. I did not link them to A because they measure benign utility loss, not shallow forgetting.

versions.untested_parts: Whether unlearning brings targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance while preserving general ability, and whether simple attacks fail to recover it.
Fine-tuning recovery of targeted forgotten knowledge from unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples. The study fine-tunes on benign prompts that expose collateral knowledge holes.
Activation-direction ablation or evidence that targeted knowledge remains present but inaccessible.
Recovery of targeted knowledge by low-bit quantization.
Recovery of targeted knowledge by prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A method that resists the recovery attacks described in the claim.

relation.reason: Only the mitigation experiment (Tables 3, 8) bears on B. The rest is collateral-loss evaluation. A reader could also call this discusses.

tranche.reason: The study measures collateral knowledge loss. Its one-shot mitigation gives a harmscore revival result bearing on B in a new setting. The reader's T6 undersells it.

source_check.notes: The B evidence is one mitigation experiment on LoRA-LLMU Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 (step 800). The pretrained model's harmscore on the forget set is not stated. The mitigation section does not say what the KL objective is computed against, but elsewhere (GAKL) KL is to the pretrained model, so the 0.90 may partly come from distilling the original. Relearning prompts are adjacent plus latent benign prompts, not purely unrelated ones.

statements.correction: LLMU-unlearned Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 (PKU-SafeRLHF forget set), one-shot KL fine-tuning on DAP (adjacent benign prompts from forget-set keywords) plus DLP-used (latent RL-found prompts), both filtered to exclude content answerable from the forget set: harmscore on the forget set 0.00 -> 0.90 (Table 3; 0.80-0.90 over steps 600-1000, Table 8). Same data with GD: 0.00 -> 0.10.
statements.problem: Cites r18 as fine-tuning on data unrelated to the forgotten topic. The relearning set is DAP (benign prompts built from forget-set keywords, so loosely related) plus DLP-used (RL-found latent prompts on broader topics). The measure is harmscore, not accuracy. This study's Mistral/PKU-SafeRLHF setting is missing from the conditions list.

statements.correction: LLMU Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, one-shot fine-tuning on benign hole prompts: GD harmscore 0.00 -> 0.10 (0.08-0.12 over steps), KL 0.00 -> 0.90.
Same LLMU model and benign prompts: KL gives harmscore 0.90, GD gives 0.10 (Tables 3, 8). Single run, no uncertainty stated.

Table 1: MMLU 0.535 -> 0.512/0.516/0.536 (LLMU/GAKL/NPOGD), 0.585 -> 0.574 (RMU). ARC-easy 0.799 -> 0.692/0.725/0.770, 0.813 -> 0.812 (RMU). TruthfulQA rises for the PKU methods (0.560 -> 0.581-0.607) and is flat for RMU (0.553). RMU DAP 7.848 -> 4.495. Up to 98.7% score-1 responses (RMU DLP).
statements.problem: The cited numbers are right, but 'MMLU/ARC/TruthfulQA barely move' overstates. ARC-easy falls 0.799 -> 0.692 under LLMU and 0.799 -> 0.725 under GAKL, and the authors call the differences 'only modest'.
